title: Geometric stalks of finite locally constant sheaves of sets are finite
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of sets on its small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Assume $\mathcal F$ is *finite locally constant*: there is a jointly surjective etale covering $\{u_i:U_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ and, for each $i$, a finite set $S_i$ and an isomorphism of sheaves $\mathcal F|_{U_i}\cong\underline{S_i}$ on $(U_i)_{\Et}$, where $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ is the restriction $V\mapsto\mathcal F(V)$ for $V\to U_i$ etale, viewed over $Y$ through $u_i$, and $\underline{S_i}$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value $S_i$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then for every geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, the geometric stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is a finite set. This includes the case $S_i=\varnothing$.

source.place: Definition Tag 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant), sets part (4); Lemma Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), part (3), for stalks under restriction; Remark Tag 03P5 (remark-constant-locally-constant-maps), constant sheaves of sets (the argument there is written for groups and uses no group operation). The finite-stalk consequence is agent-formulated.
